raw_response:
My land is only 1.7 mu, so I don't have much room to waste money, but I also can't afford a bad harvest — with just 2 of us and some off-farm income, this maize is still part of what we eat and sell. I've been doing spring maize here for many years and I mostly follow what worked last year.

For seed, I buy hybrid seed from the dealer in town — Zhengdan or one of the Xianyu numbers, whatever he has that neighbors said did well last year. Traditional seed gives poor yield, no one around here plants that anymore. One bag is plenty for 1.7 mu, maybe 1.5 kg of seed.

For fertilizer, at planting I put down compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind), about 40 kg on my plot — that's roughly 25 kg per mu as base. Then at the big trumpet stage (around the 10-12 leaf), I topdress urea, maybe 15-17 kg per mu. That gives me around 18-20 kg of pure nitrogen per mu total, 7-8 kg phosphorus, 7-8 kg potassium. This is what I've done for years. I'd rather put a little extra urea than see yellow leaves — the cost of one extra bag is small compared to losing grain.

Irrigation: spring is dry here, so I water before planting to get the seed up, then once at jointing, once at tasseling, once at grain filling if no rain. About 3-4 times with my well.

Pesticide: I spray once for armyworm/corn borer around whorl stage, and once more if aphids come at tasseling. Herbicide once after planting for weeds. So 2-3 sprays total.

Tillage: I pay the tractor man to rotary till before planting — cheaper than ploughing and fine for this soil.

Yield: last year I got about 580 kg/mu. If weather is normal I expect similar, maybe 600.
